structural-causal.name: bottleneck-control
structural-causal.basis: Large installed base, procedure growth and recurring instruments/accessories tie platform adoption to utilization economics.

structural-causal.name: scenario-robustness
structural-causal.basis: Utilization loop is resilient to individual system-placement timing, but access/reimbursement, tariffs and competing robotic platforms can slow conversion.

structural-causal.name: substitution-resilience
structural-causal.basis: Workflow integration and installed base create switching friction, but alternative robotic and non-robotic minimally invasive approaches remain substitutes.

discovery-weak-signals.name: robotic-surgery platform adoption
discovery-weak-signals.basis: Procedure growth, installed-base growth and rising system placements reinforce recurring utilization and platform expansion evidence.

adversarial-red-team.name: financing-dilution
adversarial-red-team.basis: Q1 ended with $7.98B cash/investments and included $1.1B repurchases; no financing stress is evidenced here.

adversarial-red-team.name: demand-concentration
adversarial-red-team.basis: Broad procedure adoption supports resilience, but U.S. procedure growth slowed and access policy can affect volumes.

adversarial-red-team.name: margin-fragility
adversarial-red-team.basis: 2026 outlook explicitly includes tariff drag and warns additional tariffs could be material.

expectations-execution.name: expectation conversion
expectations-execution.basis: Q1 operating performance supported a modest upward revision to procedure-growth expectations and higher da Vinci 5 placements year over year.

items.risk: Procedure and installed-base growth do not by themselves establish valuation attractiveness or uninterrupted margin expansion.
Tariffs and product mix can pressure gross margin even if procedure adoption remains strong; the prior outlook explicitly incorporated tariff impact.
A successor bottleneck can migrate from system availability to trained clinicians, hospital budgets, reimbursement/access, or procedure-specific clinical evidence.
Procedure growth can decelerate even while installed base expands, weakening utilization economics.
Lease-heavy placements can defer economic realization and increase dependence on subsequent procedure utilization.
Competition or evidence showing inferior procedure economics would weaken switching-friction assumptions.
